articles.title: Nagaland floats Rs 21.2-cr plan to strengthen chopper network
articles.description: Proposed project includes 10 new helipads, fuel stationsMorung Express News Dimapur | August 5The Nagaland Government has initiated a Rs 21.2-crore project to strengthen the State's civil aviation infrastructure by developing a network of new helipads, upgrading existing facilities and establishing aviation fuel stations to enhance passenger connectivity, emergency response and tourism.The Transport Department's A.I.R. Cell on July 17 issued a Notice Inviting e-Tender (NIT), floating a Request for Proposal (RFP) for the “Establishment of Helipads for Enhanced Helicopter Service Connectivity in Nagaland.” The proposed project, under the Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) mode and estimated at Rs 21.20 crore, is to be completed within 24 months of the award of work.According to the RFP, Nagaland introduced helicopter services in 2007 to provide safe, efficient and rapid transportation for passengers, emergency medical evacuation, disaster management, VVIP movement, tourism and other essential services. Since then, demand for helicopter services, both within and outside the State, has increased substantially.However, the document noted that existing aviation infrastructure remains inadequate to support growing operational requirements, citing an acute shortage of helipad facilities and allied infrastructure. The project seeks to address these constraints by strengthening intra-state helicopter services, improving access to remote areas, increasing operational capacity and service frequency, and promoting tourism through faster and more convenient air connectivity.New helipads, refuelling stationsThe proposal envisages construction of 10 new helipads, including seven at sub-divisional headquarters: Tening, Tuli, Tobu, Pungro, Bhandari, Mangkolemba and Tamlu.Three additional helipads are proposed at the tourist destinations of Doyang, Longwa and Dzukou.The project also includes upgrading existing helipads at Lower Tizu, Aitepyong, Shilloi and Satakha.Besides helipad infrastructure, the project proposes establishing Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF) refuelling stations at Chümoukedima Heliport and the helipads at Mon and Kiphire.These facilities are intended to improve operational capacity and increase helicopter service frequency by reducing refuelling constraints, the RFP stated.Passenger facilitiesThe proposed helipads are designed as passenger service facilities rather than simple landing sites.Each new location will include a 30-metre-diameter helipad, an 84.3 sq m waiting hall comprising a waiting lounge, reception, office, security checking area, VIP lounge, toilets for men, women and persons with disabilities, separate entry and exit points with ramps, electrification, sanitary works and rainwater harvesting facilities.The scope of work also includes approach roads, parking yards, side drains, culverts, boundary fencing with gates and fire safety provisions.Existing helicopter networkThe infrastructure expansion builds on Nagaland's existing helicopter service, which currently operates two helicopters under a four-year Memorandum of Understanding with M/s Thumby Aviation Pvt Ltd, effective from January 10, 2024.According to the Transport Department, the service connects 20 sectors across the State through scheduled weekly operations while also providing charter services for patient evacuation, emergency response, VIP and VVIP movement, bank remittances and other State requirements. The State helicopter service operates under subsidised and non-subsidised categories, with passengers travelling to district headquarters and those requiring medical evacuation paying only 25% of the notified fare, while charter services for VIPs, corporate clients and private individuals are charged at full rates.Last year, the government also introduced a daily weekday helicopter service between Dimapur and Kohima to facilitate travel amid road connectivity challenges on the corridor.Meanwhile, the tender closes on August 11, with technical bids scheduled to be opened the same day.

articles.title: Gujarat govt imposes statewide ban on glue traps, citing animal cruelty
articles.description: Gandhinagar, Aug 4 (IANS) The Gujarat government has imposed an immediate statewide ban on the production, sale, storage and use of glue traps, commonly known as sticky boards, used to catch rats and other small animals, making the devices illegal across the state as part of a move to prevent cruelty to animals. The decision was announced through a resolution issued by the state's Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Cooperation Department. The ban applies to the manufacture, sale, purchase, storage and use of glue traps with immediate effect. Glue traps are coated with a highly adhesive, non-drying substance that immobilises animals and birds on contact. According to the government, trapped animals often sustain serious injuries while attempting to escape and may eventually die from starvation, dehydration, suffocation or injuries caused during their struggle. The government said the use of glue traps violates Section 11(1) of the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960. It also noted that the Animal Welfare Board of India has classified the use of glue traps as highly cruel and illegal under its guidelines. In a parallel measure, the Industries and Mines Department has directed that glue traps be removed with immediate effect from the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) procurement portal as well as from other e-commerce and online platforms. The order also prohibits all government departments, boards, corporations and local self-government bodies from purchasing or using the devices. The resolution warns that any violation of the ban may attract legal action under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, and Section 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, along with any other applicable provisions of law. District Police authorities and the Society for Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (SPCA) have been authorised to register complaints and initiate action against those found violating the prohibition. The government has directed traders to immediately stop stocking and selling glue traps, as their production, sale, purchase and storage are now prohibited. It has also advised members of the public not to use glue traps for rodent control in homes, offices or factories. Instead, citizens have been encouraged to adopt legally approved and animal-friendly alternatives, including cage traps and other non-lethal rodent control methods, in place of adhesive traps. --IANS mys/dan
